claims.claim: For any continuous g, the response set at fixed mean is a closed attained interval [lower convex envelope, upper concave envelope].
claims.evidence: Document sections 2.1 and 2.3: compact planar convex hull and elementary affine-dependence reduction.

claims.claim: Each endpoint has an optimizer supported on at most two energies. This does not assert that all optimizers have at most two support points.
claims.evidence: Document section 2.2: interior triangle contradiction and collinear reduction.

claims.claim: Every response in the interval is attainable; a general at-most-three-point representation follows from the same planar reduction.
Under strict convexity the minimum is g(m) at unique delta_m and maximum is the endpoint chord at the unique endpoint mixture, for interior m. Endpoint means admit only their own Dirac measure.
The mono-plus-endpoint mixture gives an explicit at-most-three-line family. An anchored two-line path also attains every intermediate response by continuity and strict increase of secant slopes.
claims.evidence: Document section 3.1. Three lines are sufficient, not necessary; anchored-path uniqueness is not global representation uniqueness.

claims.claim: If endpoint signs are opposite, unique kernel root E_minus and chord root E_plus obey a<E_minus<E_plus<b and determine the five complete mean-sign regimes, including unique zero extremizers at both boundaries.
The actual PHYS24 coefficient interval and sign partition follow for the fixed serialized J after consuming the separate curvature and endpoint sign certificate.
claims.evidence: Document section 6.1; no replay or independent curvature verification claimed.
